title: Objective summit — divine authority; formal reason is revelation
source_text: XX. Hanc esse summam atque absolutam, ac, ut diximus, ipsam scientiarum certitudinem superare, ex eo probant Theologi, quod fundamentum quo nititur est ipsa authoritas & veritas divina, qua nihil est magis firmum, atque immutabile, & quod minus fallere possit. Nam ratio propria &, ut Scholae loquuntur, formalis, cur credendis fides assentitur, est divinum testimonium, seu divina revelatio. Nempe hunc & illum articulum credimus, verbi causa, in Deo tres esse personas distinctas, & Christum esse Deum & hominem in una persona, quoniam istud Deus dixit & revelavit in verbo Evangelii.
pass_a_gloss: That this is the highest and absolute, and, as we have said, surpasses even the certainty of the sciences, the Theologians prove from this: that the foundation on which it rests is the very divine authority and truth, than which nothing is more firm and immutable, and which can less deceive. For the proper reason, and as the Schools speak the formal reason, why faith assents to things to be believed, is the divine testimony, or divine revelation. Namely we believe this and that article — for example that in God there are three distinct persons, and that Christ is God and man in one person — because God has said and revealed that in the word of the Gospel.
pass_b_english: Foundation: divine authority/truth — firmer, less able to deceive.
Formal reason of assent: divine testimony/revelation (Trinity; Christ God-man — because God said it in the Gospel).

lemmas.gloss: the divine testimony, or divine revelation

choices.term: ratio … formalis, cur credendis fides assentitur, est divinum testimonium
choices.english: the formal reason why faith assents to things to be believed is the divine testimony
choices.why: States School formal ratio before XXI’s scruple.
rejected: faith assents formally because of moral signs alone
